$comment: CUTOVER (B5/F6). The legacy app is STILL DEPLOYED and still the default.
The new React app is built to frontend/dist and served at /v2. Nothing is
deleted: flipping the last route from /index.html to /frontend/dist/index.html
makes v2 the default, and reverting that single line rolls back. Deleting the
legacy files in the cutover commit would make rollback a restore instead of a
revert, which is the difference between one minute and one afternoon.
Both apps talk to the same /api, so a user bounced back to the legacy app
after a rollback loses no data — only the newer screens.

headers.$comment: No camera: the OCR/scanning features are dropped, so nothing needs it.
